samples.summary: scrubCss's url() regex nulls legitimate quoted fragment references (`url("#id")`) because the optional quote group backtracks past the `(?!#)` guard
samples.evidence: `/url\(\s*(['"]?)(?!#)[^)]*\1\s*\)/gi` is intended to keep same-document `url(#…)` refs. For `url("#grad")` the engine first matches group 1 = `"`, then `(?!#)` fails at `#`; it then backtracks group 1 to the empty string, at which point `(?!#)` succeeds (next char is `"`), `[^)]*` consumes `"#grad"`, `\1` matches empty and the whole thing is replaced with `none`. So any quoted fragment reference in a mermaid `<style>` block or a `style` attribute (gradients, patterns, clip-path, markers) is silently destroyed, while the unquoted form survives — the opposite of the documented intent. Fix: anchor the negative lookahead after the quote, e.g. `url\(\s*(?:"(?!#)[^")]*"|'(?!#)[^')]*'|(?!#)[^'")]*)\s*\)`.

samples.summary: Failures are cached permanently per (theme, source), so a diagram that fails for a non-deterministic reason never gets another attempt while the note text is unchanged
samples.evidence: `remember(key, result)` stores `{error}` in the same LRU as successes, and `collectPending()` applies a cached error synchronously on every later render. The comment argues a failure is "a deterministic property of the source" because passes are serialized, but that only rules out inter-pass races: `mermaid.render()` can also fail from causes unrelated to the source (e.g. a partially-loaded diagram-type chunk after a transient network error — mermaid's per-type modules are themselves `import()`ed, `maxTextSize`/`maxEdges` interactions, or an exception from mermaid's global state). Once cached, the only way to retry is to edit the fence text or toggle the theme; a reload of the preview will not do it because the cache is module-global and never invalidated. Consider caching only successes, or evicting error entries after a short TTL / on engine reload.

samples.summary: The new `if (currentViewMode !== 'edit') renderPreview()` guard does not achieve what its comment and test claim: the preview (and therefore the mermaid engine) is already rendered on every keystroke even in 'edit' mode
samples.evidence: editor.ts:443 skips the repaint when the preview is hidden, and editor.test.ts justifies it as avoiding "download[ing] the mermaid engine for a pane nobody is looking at". But the CodeMirror updateListener at editor.ts:326 (`if (u.docChanged) renderPreview();`) fires regardless of view mode, and `applyViewMode` also calls `renderPreview()` on show. So in 'edit' mode the first keystroke re-renders the hidden preview, emits mermaid placeholders and kicks `renderMermaidBlocks`, loading and laying out the engine for the hidden pane anyway. The guard is therefore only a partial optimisation and the invariant asserted by the test does not hold in the real flow (the test only proves the setTheme path, never dispatching a doc change).

samples.summary: A note with more than RENDER_CACHE_LIMIT (40) diagrams thrashes the cache, so every keystroke re-lays out every diagram on the page — the exact cost the cache exists to prevent
samples.evidence: `remember()` evicts the oldest entry whenever `renderCache.size > 40`. With N > 40 pending blocks in one pass, entries cached earlier in the *same* `renderPass` loop are evicted before the loop ends, so the next `render()` (one per keystroke in split mode) finds nothing cached and serially re-runs `mermaid.render()` for all N diagrams. Because passes are serialized on `passChain`, that also means the newest pass waits behind a full N-diagram layout, freezing diagram updates for as long as it takes. The limit is a fixed constant with no relation to the number of blocks actually on the page.

samples.summary: stripConfigDirectives drops the entire YAML front matter when it contains a `config:` key, discarding legitimate sibling keys such as `title:` / `displayMode:`
samples.evidence:
`if (frontmatter && /^\s*config\s*:/m.test(frontmatter[1])) stripped = stripped.slice(frontmatter[0].length);` removes the whole `---…---` block, not just the `config:` mapping. A diagram written as `---
title: Sales
config:
  theme: forest
---` loses its title as well, so the rendered diagram silently differs from what the author wrote even though only the config part is unsafe. Stripping just the `config:` block (or re-emitting the front matter without it) would preserve the benign keys.

samples.summary: Reusing a cached SVG for two identical fences in one note injects duplicate element ids into the document
samples.evidence: `apply()` assigns the memoized `result.svg` verbatim, and the cache is keyed only by `theme + source`. A note containing the same diagram twice therefore gets two DOM subtrees carrying the same mermaid-generated ids (root `id="note-mermaid-N"` plus its internal marker/gradient/clip ids), and the `<style>` block mermaid scopes with `#note-mermaid-N` plus every `url(#…)` reference now resolves ambiguously (first match wins). The content is identical so it usually renders the same, but the document invariant "ids are unique" is broken and any future per-instance styling/interaction keyed off those ids will target the wrong node.

samples.summary: SAFE_URL_RE rejects `data:` and relative URLs, so image/icon-bearing diagram types lose their images silently rather than degrading to source
samples.evidence: `URL_ATTRS.has(name) && !SAFE_URL_RE.test(...)` removes `href`/`xlink:href`/`src` unless the value starts with `#`, `http(s)://` or `mailto:`. Mermaid emits `` / `` for icon shapes and architecture-diagram icons (and `xlink:href` with relative refs in a few renderers). Those attributes are stripped after the engine has already succeeded, so the block shows a rendered-but-broken diagram (empty icon boxes) with no error message and no source fallback. Allowing `data:image/` (or at least labelling the block) would keep the documented "never blank / always readable" property.

samples.summary: When the engine fails to load, blocks stay `data-mermaid-pending` forever with no user-visible signal, and every subsequent keystroke queues a no-op pass onto the shared chain
samples.evidence: `if (!mermaid || superseded()) return;` leaves the placeholder pending and un-labelled. `loaded` is memoized as a resolved `null` and never retried, so each later `render()` re-collects the same blocks, chains a pass on `passChain`, and does nothing. Behaviour is intentional per the docstring, but the user sees raw source with no hint that the diagram engine failed, and there is no way to retry short of a page reload.
